trust_decision.summary: Lookyloo decides whether attacker-uploaded compressed capture data (base64 gzip HAR in JSON, or a full-capture ZIP and the gzip HAR inside it) is small enough to decompress into memory; at the pinned commit no size bound exists at the decompression calls.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Capture Upload'; /json/upload is the upload API and its gzip.decompress on the base64 HAR is the obvious decompression call.

fix_sites.module_kind: core library method (Lookyloo.unpack_full_capture_archive), ZIP total-size check

fix_sites.module_kind: core library method, nested gzip decompression

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The stored multiple-downloads ZIP is the capture's own downloaded-file artefact that is served back to analysts on request, not something decompressed during upload, so a solver could argue it is a download feature outside the 'capture upload' scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The legacy uncompressed HAR must still be accepted: when the data is not gzip, the code falls back to the raw bytes (old format). Legitimate large-but-sane exports must also still unpack. A fix that rejects all non-gzip data, or sets a very small limit, breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: base64 gzip HAR in the JSON body (genericapi.py:815)
deflated entries in the full-capture ZIP, bounded by total declared size (fix.diff:98-100)

O7_producer.where: lookyloo/lookyloo.py:2449-2455 (store_capture writes uploaded 0.data/0.data.filename verbatim); consumer lookyloo/lookyloo.py:1636-1645

O8_uncovered_routes.route: An uploaded capture (full-capture ZIP 0.data plus 0.data.filename, or the Lacus-format JSON downloaded_file/downloaded_filename with a chosen uuid) can store a nested ZIP named '<uuid>_multiple_downloads.zip'. get_data(index_in_zip) later reads one entry fully into memory with no size bound.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The decompression happens at download time, not upload time, inside a 'downloaded files' feature. It is also legitimately produced by real captures.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Same file as the unpack site but a different method, reached from other routes: website/web/__init__.py:1146-1150 (/tree/<uuid>/get_downloaded_file) and website/web/__init__.py:2035-2038 (Pandora submit). The producers are genericapi.py:849-857 and lookyloo/lookyloo.py:2334-2337.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The Lacus-format branch of /json/upload accepts downloaded_file and stores it unchecked. This is the same producer as above, but it bypasses unpack_full_capture_archive and its new total-size check entirely.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: There is no decompression in this branch itself. The data is only base64-decoded and written to disk.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Same file as the landing point, a third branch of the same handler

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Trusted-timestamp validation gunzips the stored HAR with gzip.decompress. A planted variant could read an uploaded raw gz artefact instead.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The stored HAR is re-gzipped by store_capture (lookyloo/lookyloo.py:2461-2463), so a maintainer could easily add another stored gz artefact (e.g. html.gz) and decompress it unbounded at this spot.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The MISP export gunzips the stored HAR. A sibling that accepts a gz storage/frames file from upload and decompresses it here would be realistic.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same gzip.decompress idiom is already used for exports, and new optional artefacts are added to the archive format regularly (see lookyloo/lookyloo.py:2340-2348).

O9_family: resource exhaustion: unbounded decompression (zip/gzip bomb), CWE-400/CWE-409

services: Lacus or playwrightcapture for live captures (not needed for upload)
O10_build.project_tests: Only tests/test_generic.py, a Playwright UI smoke test that needs a running instance and network capture of google.fr; nothing covers upload or decompression.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Bound the gzip.decompress in the /json/upload har_file branch only, leaving the full-capture ZIP unpack and the stored nested-ZIP download path unbounded.

out_of_scope_notes: submit_capture pull_capture_domain fetches an arbitrary remote Lookyloo instance (website/web/__init__.py:2306-2318, 2328-2334); it may be an SSRF-type concern, not pursued.
Request body size for raw HAR upload (website/web/__init__.py:2347) is a plain size concern, not decompression; not pursued.
unverified: Lessons-v2 records resource-exhaustion tasks as 0 of 7 hard. This host is DoS-family, which is the main weakness of the pick, though it is not one of the defined O12 flags.

Whether CPython's ZipExtFile truncates output to the declared central-directory file_size, which would make the fix's total_size check sound against lying headers, was not checked in the stdlib source.

Whether the nested downloads ZIP is reachable with an attacker-chosen filename on the full-capture route also depends on the 'uuid' entry not colliding (lookyloo/lookyloo.py:2310-2318 reassigns the uuid on collision); on the Lacus JSON route the uuid is caller-supplied (website/web/genericapi.py:797).
